close_reason: Added two probe tests on Name (the canonical wire-format struct in this crate): name_at_type_populates_at_type_not_extras and name_at_type_and_vendor_extras_coexist_separately. Both verify the @type-vs-extras serde interaction empirically and pass on serde 1.x. The parent JMAP-sgrr epic's lowest-confidence-area concern is now an empirically-verified property. 61 tests pass; clippy + cargo doc -D warnings clean. The probes are deliberately on Name only — that's enough to verify the serde behavior; all 23 in-scope structs share the identical attribute shape, so a Name probe is representative.
description: Every Deserialize struct in lib.rs combines two serde features whose interaction is the source of well-known bugs: #[serde(rename = "@type", ...)] on at_type AND #[serde(flatten)] on extra: serde_json::Map. The intended behaviour is: a wire object containing @type populates at_type and leaves extra empty. The pathological alternative is: serde flatten captures @type into extra and at_type stays None. Test coverage gap: 0 of 58 tests feed an input containing @type. The fixtures at lib.rs:1184-1554 are taken verbatim from RFC 9553 figures which omit @type for defaultType cases, and the assert_extras_roundtrip helper at lib.rs:1581 also omits @type. The only test that exercises @type is anniversary_date_unknown_preserves_opaque at lib.rs:1486, which exercises a custom Deserialize impl, not the derive-based path. Probe (file for /do-beads): write a unit test for one struct (e.g. Name) with input json!({"@type":"Name","full":"X"}), assert (a) name.at_type == Some("Name".to_owned()), (b) name.extra is empty, (c) re-serialize equals input. Repeat for one struct with both @type AND a vendor-extra key, to confirm @type does not leak into extras when extras is non-empty. If the probe fails, the fix is a serde version constraint or a custom Deserialize impl; if it passes, the test catches future regressions when serde-derive or serde-flatten internals change.
title: No round-trip test asserts @type wire field lands on at_type (not in extras)
